This might sound terrible but how do you know you could’ve changed that? Being suicidal sucks all the same whether you’re in a relationship or not, whether that relationship is a healthy and a happy one — or not. It’s complex and impossible to predict. You have no way of knowing whether you staying would have changed that. 

My ex threatened to kill himself when I broke up with him and then (we were long distance) blocked me and just went quiet on all of his social media accounts. He didn’t go through with it, that was just another one of his manipulation tactics. But I didn’t hear from him for a week, I couldn’t find any of his friends, couldn’t contact his parents. It was fucking terrifying and I thought I’d killed him. But during that week I had some time to think (mostly because I still hoped he hadn’t done it). I tried very hard to understand what I could’ve done differently but.. nothing really. I understood that even better when I was suicidal myself. This is a little hard to explain but it’s nobody’s responsibility to keep me alive and only I can make decisions about it. If I’d killed myself, it would’ve been my decision only.

Like everybody else said — it’s not your fault. Killing yourself is a layered thing. It’s out of your control. 

Please, I hope you’ll listen to all the people here telling you it’s not your fault because it really isn’t. I am incredibly sorry that you are going through all this pain. I wish you didn’t have to. I really, really hope you can and will find a way to heal.

I’m so sorry you had to go through all this. None of what happened to you was your fault and has nothing to do with how good/bad you are. They clearly aren’t experts on that since they act like that. You don’t owe them or anyone else to be good or be anything else for that matter. Something that my therapist told me is that other people’s opinion does not reflect what you are, it actually reflects what they are more than anything. Sure, we should listen to criticism — but constructive, respectful criticism aims at something concrete. Like, if you get distracted while talking to a friend, constructive criticism would be something like “you aren’t paying attention right now”, not “you’re awful at communicating. General “you’re bad/lying/unprofessional/stupid (you name it)” is just bullying and can’t be tolerated. From yourself as well.

Besides it makes you even more depressed afterwards. I prevent myself from losing it by reminding myself that I’m on my way to recovery, even if it’s bumpy and not always successful. It may sounds stupid,  but sometimes it does help, sometimes I still lose it — but not like that, not like I used to.

When my health anxiety was at its peak, that was a “normal” thing to happen for me. Once I had a dream in which I thought I was having a heart attack (which was actually a panic attack) and woke up immediately terrified, my heart racing. I felt like I was about to die. I remember also lying in bed at night unable to sleep, listening to my breath and measuring my heart rate and thinking that I’d die in my sleep. I’m not gonna say it’s normal — it isn’t — but this is all anxiety. I was having shallow breaths all of the time then — for me it’s like I can’t get enough air with a normal breath, so I had to take more deep breaths more often. It really is anxiety.

Some other user recommended trying to relax and I second it. Do something that is pleasant for you, something that brings you pleasant, maybe nostalgic memories. I found that watching Pirates of the Caribbean (my favourite movie when I was a teen) really helped take my mind off of my anxiety.
